title: API 580 Training in Billings, MT: RBI Exam Prep Online
description: API 580 exam prep for Billings and Laurel RBI teams: self-paced online with instructor Q&A, covering RP 580, Montana's rules and river-side consequence.
h1: API 580 Training in Billings, Montana: Online Exam Prep for Risk-Based Inspection Teams
html:
API 580 exam prep for risk-based inspection work in Yellowstone County

Risk-based inspection is how many refineries decide where inspection effort goes, and the Billings area has three of them sharing one river valley. API 580 is the certification for the people who build, run and audit those programmes: inspection planners, corrosion and materials engineers, reliability engineers and the contract specialists who support them. It is a single closed-book examination of 90 multiple-choice questions, 80 of them scored and 10 unscored pretest items, in 3 hours and 15 minutes. API's 2026 Body of Knowledge names one reference, API RP 580, Elements of a Risk-Based Inspection Program, fourth edition (August 2023) with Addenda 1 (March 2025), and groups the questions into ten categories from terms and definitions to RBI documentation.

Atlantis NDT prepares candidates for that examination with a self-paced online course and an instructor who answers questions. You enrol and start straight away. There is no Atlantis classroom in Billings. API, which administers the exam and certifies those who pass, now lets you schedule API 580 either at a test centre or through remote proctoring, so a Billings candidate may not need to travel at all.

Who sits API 580 around Billings

Many API 580 candidates already hold an API inspector certificate. A current API 510, API 570 or API 653 certification qualifies you automatically, and many refinery inspectors take API 580 once they find themselves planning inspections rather than only performing them. Others come to it through engineering or reliability roles and qualify on education and petrochemical industry experience gained in the last 10 years: one year with a bachelor's degree, two with a two-year degree, three with a high school diploma and five or more without formal education.

Roles that bring people in and around Billings to API 580 include:

  • refinery inspection planners and coordinators who maintain inspection plans and due dates;
  • materials and corrosion engineers who write damage mechanism reviews and corrosion loops;
  • reliability and process safety staff who sit on an RBI team or audit its output;
  • staff of contract inspection and engineering firms that support RBI work for refinery and pipeline clients;
  • pipeline and terminal integrity staff who manage tanks and want to understand where risk methods can and cannot be used for them.

Three rulebooks on one refinery site

An RBI programme in Billings works inside three different sets of rules, and a candidate who knows how they divide understands what an RBI result can actually change.

Pressure vessels and process piping. Montana is not an OSHA State Plan state, so federal process safety management applies to the refineries, and its mechanical integrity element asks for inspection and testing that follows recognised and generally accepted good engineering practice. EPA's Risk Management Program rule says the same for Program 3 processes in 40 CFR 68.73. Montana's boiler rules state that the boiler law gives the Department of Labor and Industry no jurisdiction over unfired pressure vessels, so no state vessel schedule competes with the owner's programme. Within that programme, API 510 and API 570 both allow intervals to be set by an RBI assessment; API 510's interval clauses apply unless an RBI assessment justifies something else.

Boilers. Montana's boiler law, Title 50, chapter 74, covers boilers and steam engines, includes a section on required inspection intervals, and lets the department accept inspections by special boiler inspectors from insurance companies who hold National Board certificates. An RBI study can rank a boiler alongside everything else for planning, but it cannot move a statutory inspection date; the statute leaves longer intervals to the department, on written application.

Pipeline breakout tanks. Under 49 CFR 195.432(b), operators inspect atmospheric and low-pressure steel breakout tanks to API 653, but the risk-based internal inspection procedures in section 6.4.3 of API 653 cannot be used to set the internal inspection interval. For breakout tankage, then, the internal inspection interval is outside the reach of an RBI result, however good the model.

A river along every fence: consequence in the Billings plants

RP 580 treats consequence of failure as more than fire and explosion. Safety and health, environmental and business or financial consequences all belong in the assessment, and the environmental part depends on where a release can go. In Billings that question has an obvious answer, because Montana DEQ's own fact sheets put the Yellowstone River beside each refinery:

  • the Phillips 66 refinery covers about 200 acres on the south-east side of Billings, with the river roughly 1,000 feet to the east and groundwater flowing north-east towards it;
  • the former ExxonMobil refinery, now Par Montana's, has its processing area bounded to the north by the Yellowstone;
  • at CHS in Laurel, the river borders the southern part of the refinery property.

The DEQ description of the Phillips 66 site, clay-silts over sandy gravels on an alluvial terrace with shale bedrock about 22 feet down, is the kind of detail an environmental consequence model needs. A liquid release on permeable ground near a river is a different consequence from the same release on clay far from water, and an RBI team that uses a generic environmental factor misses the point of the site. For the exam, learn how RP 580 separates the consequence categories, how it describes the use of consequence results to decide between inspection and mitigation, and why consequence, unlike probability, is rarely changed by inspecting.

When the crude, the unit or the owner changes

RP 580 expects an RBI assessment to be updated when the things it was built on change. Montana refining has seen all three kinds of change that matter:

  • Feed. When Phillips 66 took its Billings refinery down for a turnaround in 2017, BIC Magazine reported that a vacuum improvement project being tied in would, company officials said, let the plant handle up to 100 percent heavy Canadian crude, against the mix of heavy, high-sulfur Canadian crude and domestic crudes it was then running. A shift in crude slate changes sulfur, acid and chloride levels, and with them the damage mechanisms and rates an assessment depends on.
  • Service. At Great Falls, Calumet's Montana Renewables created its biorefinery by reconfiguring an oversized mild hydrotreater at the refinery to process renewable feedstocks, alongside the conventional refinery and specialty asphalt plant. In November 2026 Calumet said Calumet Montana Refining had signed a long-term lease with Montana Renewables for more installed equipment at Great Falls, including a hydrotreater, a hydrogen plant and a naphtha splitter, to be repurposed for a sustainable aviation fuel expansion. A unit in new service is, for RBI purposes, a new unit with a history that no longer fully applies.
  • Ownership. Par Pacific took over the Billings refinery from ExxonMobil in June 2023 with its pipelines, terminals and storage. Whenever records, procedures and software move between owners, the data behind any risk ranking has to be checked before it is trusted.

The exam does not ask about any of these plants. It asks what should trigger a reassessment, what data must be revalidated, and how management of change connects to the RBI programme, and local examples like these make the RP 580 text far easier to remember in a closed-book room.

A closed-book exercise: ranking items before a five-yearly turnaround

BIC Magazine reported in 2017 that the Phillips 66 refinery in Billings went through a full turnaround every five years. Picture an inspection planner at a refinery on that kind of cycle with three items whose risk the RBI model projects to pass the site's risk target before the next one.

  1. A hot gas oil line with a high probability of failure and uncertain data. Its last thickness survey was sparse. The RP 580 answer is that inspection lowers risk by reducing uncertainty about the damage state; a well-chosen on-stream survey now may show the probability is lower than assumed, or confirm that a replacement must be planned.
  2. An amine regenerator overhead drum with cracking as its credible mechanism. Its last inspection was visual. Inspection effectiveness depends on matching the technique to the mechanism, so another visual inspection adds little confidence; an examination capable of finding cracks is what changes the assessed probability.
  3. A large-inventory item next to the river with modest probability. Here the risk is driven by consequence, and inspecting more will not change the consequence. The options RP 580 points to are mitigation: reducing inventory, improving isolation or containment, or changing the process.

These are the distinctions the probability, consequence and risk management categories of the Body of Knowledge cover: which lever lowers probability, which lowers consequence, and when inspection on its own does not help. Most of the work is knowing the RP 580 vocabulary well enough that the right answer stands out from three plausible ones.

How to read RP 580 for a closed-book paper

With one reference and no books in the room, the exam is a test of how well you know RP 580 itself. A study plan that works for most Billings candidates follows the ten Body of Knowledge categories:

  • start with terms, definitions and acronyms, since many questions turn on the exact meaning of probability of failure, consequence of failure, risk target and inspection effectiveness;
  • move to risk assessment and the RBI programme: qualitative, semi-quantitative and quantitative approaches, the risk matrix and how results are presented;
  • cover roles, responsibilities, training and qualifications, then data collection, so you know who on the team supplies what and what happens when data is missing;
  • work through damage mechanisms, probability of failure and consequence of failure as RP 580 frames them;
  • finish with risk management and RBI documentation, including reassessment and the records an audit expects.

RP 581, the quantitative method, is not a reference publication for the exam. Inspectors who use RP 581-based software at work should be careful not to answer from the software's logic when the question is about RP 580's principles. In the self-paced course, send the instructor any definition that two parts of RP 580 seem to use differently; those are the points that cost marks.

Exam preparation or an RBI study for your plant?

They are different jobs, and it helps to keep them apart. The course prepares individuals to pass API 580 and to work competently on an RBI team. A site that needs an assessment built, revalidated or audited needs a study, with its own data, team and documentation. Atlantis also carries out risk-based inspection studies delivered remotely, working from the owner's data, with intervals approved by the owner's inspector of record; that service is separate from the course and is quoted separately.

Sponsoring API 580 candidates from Billings employers

Refineries, inspection contractors and pipeline operators can enrol several API 580 candidates together, and fees are quoted on request. Because the exam can be remote-proctored, a group spread across Laurel, Billings and field locations can sit it without coordinating travel, though each person still applies to API individually. Sponsors should also plan for the three-year term: an application to recertify can go in from 90 days before expiry, with a 90-day grace period that carries late fees, and API does not currently require employment verification to recertify API 580.

faq.q: Can I take the API 580 exam from home in Billings?
faq.a: API now lets candidates schedule API 580 either at an in-person test centre or through remote proctoring. Remote sittings have their own rules about the room, the computer and identification, so read API's and the proctoring provider's requirements before you choose. Either way the exam is closed-book: 90 questions in 3 hours and 15 minutes, with no references allowed.

faq.q: I already hold API 570 from my refinery job. Do I need more experience to sit API 580?
faq.a: No. A current API 510, API 570 or API 653 certification qualifies you automatically for the API 580 examination. You still submit an application to API for the exam window you want. Candidates without one of those certificates qualify on education plus petrochemical industry experience gained in the last 10 years, from one year with a bachelor's degree up to five or more without formal education.

faq.q: Is API RP 581 on the API 580 exam?
faq.a: No. API's Body of Knowledge lists one reference publication, API RP 580. RP 581 sets out the quantitative RBI method that much RBI software is built on, and RP 580 refers to quantitative approaches in general terms, but the exam questions are drawn from RP 580. If you work with RP 581-based tools, study RP 580's own wording rather than the software's terminology.

faq.q: Can an RBI assessment set inspection intervals for pressure vessels in Montana?
faq.a: Montana's boiler rules say the state has no jurisdiction over unfired pressure vessels, so vessel intervals are set within the owner's mechanical integrity programme under federal OSHA process safety management. API 510 allows the internal and external intervals to be set by an RBI assessment, subject to the code's conditions. Boilers are different: they fall under the state boiler law and its required inspection intervals, which an RBI ranking does not override.

faq.q: Does passing API 580 make me qualified to lead an RBI study?
faq.a: It shows that you know the RP 580 principles; it does not by itself make you a team leader. RP 580 describes an RBI team with defined roles, from inspection and materials specialists to process and operations people, and the owner decides who is competent to lead an assessment. Most Billings candidates use the certificate as a foundation and build the leadership experience on real assessments.

faq.q: Which edition of RP 580 should I study?
faq.a: The one in the Body of Knowledge for your exam. API's 2026 Body of Knowledge names the fourth edition of RP 580, published in August 2023, with Addenda 1 of March 2025, and says the exam focuses on the most recent edition. Check the current Body of Knowledge on API's site when you apply, in case it has been updated since.

faq.q: Can our refinery enrol several engineers and planners together?
faq.a: Yes. A refinery or contractor can put several people through the course at once, with fees quoted on request. Each person studies at their own pace and asks the instructor questions individually, which suits planners, engineers and contractors on different schedules. Everyone applies to API separately and chooses either a test centre or remote proctoring for their own sitting.
